summary: Verified new /api/restore endpoint and Backup UI restore form for local SQLite Site Expense Manager. Rewrote obsolete auth-based pytest file into a no-auth suite that covers root/dashboard/all resource endpoints, backup ZIP shape, restore round-trip, and three restore error paths. Backend: 9/9 pytest tests pass. Frontend: nav data-testids present for all 10 sidebar routes; Backup page shows Download + Restore form; POST /api/restore succeeds end-to-end returning {restored:true, transactions:20, accounts:2, sites:3} and the success banner (data-testid=backup-message) is rendered. However, the .dropzone <label> visually overlaps the 'Restore now' <button>, making the button not reliably clickable by a real user (Playwright had to click via JS to reach it).

ui_bugs.issue: The .dropzone label overlaps/covers the 'Restore now' submit button. A normal click in the button's visual area hits the label instead and re-opens the file picker; the button had to be clicked via JS to fire the form submit. Button text 'Restore now' is not visible in screenshots.

issues: Restore card layout is broken: dropzone label and helper text overflow and overlap surrounding elements (see screenshot). Suggest wrapping label + button in a proper flex column with gap and giving the dropzone a fixed height, and hiding the native file input via visually-hidden CSS instead of leaving it absolutely positioned.

action_items: Fix CSS on Backup page: prevent .dropzone label from overlapping/covering [data-testid="restore-submit-button"] so a user can actually click Restore now.
Add explicit min-height / gap on .backup-card and .dropzone so the Restore card matches the Backup card visually.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py /api/restore deletes every file under statements/ and documents/ before extracting. If the uploaded ZIP is missing those folders (e.g. a fresh backup with no receipts), local receipts still get wiped even though the DB is restored — acceptable per spec but worth documenting.
server.py catches only zipfile.BadZipFile; any other extraction error (e.g. permission, disk full) will 500 instead of returning a clean 400.

App.js Backup component uses default form <button> without type="submit" attribute — currently works because it's the only button in the form, but adding explicit type="submit" is safer if more buttons are ever added.
App.js is still a single-line minified-style file (~44 long lines) — readability remains poor; consider splitting per-route components into separate files.
server.py mounts a wildcard SPA route at /{full_path:path} which will shadow any future non-/api backend routes; fine for local Windows bundling but keep in mind.

success_rate.frontend: 90% (all testids present, restore flow works but Restore-now button is visually blocked by overlapping label)

seed_data_creation: None — used the app's existing demo seed (2 accounts, 3 sites, 12 categories, 20 transactions).
context_for_next_testing_agent: App is no-auth local SQLite ledger. Previous auth-oriented test_site_expense.py was rewritten. Backend endpoints verified: /api/, /api/dashboard, /api/accounts, /api/sites, /api/categories, /api/rules, /api/statements, /api/transactions, /api/settings, /api/backup, /api/restore. Restore round-trip is safe against the existing seed. The only outstanding issue is a CSS overlap on the Backup page hiding the 'Restore now' button — functionally the endpoint works, only the button click path is blocked visually.
rca of the issue: The Restore form is structured as <form> containing a <label class="dropzone"> (with the hidden file input inside) followed by the submit <button>. In the current CSS the .dropzone label expands to fill available height and its absolutely-positioned inner content overflows downward, covering the sibling <button>. Any click near the button hits the label first because label is above the button in z-order/DOM flow, which re-triggers the file chooser instead of submitting the form. Reproduction: open /backup, choose a ZIP, try clicking 'Restore now' visually — file picker opens again. Programmatic .click() on the button fires the submit correctly and /api/restore returns 200. Mitigation: fix .dropzone CSS (fixed height, overflow:hidden, gap between label and button), or restructure the form so the submit button sits outside the label wrapper.
